biomarkers.name: See PRIMARY_CNS_LYMPHOMA_B_CELL under B_CELL_NHL section
biomarkers.clinical_use: Usually CD20-positive large B-cell lymphoma with non-GCB/ABC phenotype in the great majority of cases. MYD88 L265P and CD79B mutations are common and enriched versus systemic DLBCL; no pathognomonic driver fusion is established for routine clinical use.

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma morphology with angiocentric growth pattern (perivascular tumour cell aggregation)
variants: DLBCL of activated B-cell (ABC)/non-GCB subtype (most common)
less common: T-cell PCNSL, Hodgkin lymphoma of CNS

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Distinctive — dense B-cell tumour infiltrate with reactive T cells and microglia/macrophages; blood-brain and blood-CSF barriers limit delivery of many systemic agents
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Angiocentric growth around blood vessels; reactive gliosis around infiltrate

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Post-germinal centre/late germinal centre B cells with tropism for the CNS microenvironment
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Mesoderm — haematopoietic (B lymphocytes) migrating to CNS
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: DLBCL of ABC/non-GCB subtype in the great majority of cases, with characteristic CNS tropism; MYD88 L265P and CD79B mutations are enriched, often fitting the MCD genetic subtype
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: See also B_CELL_NHL/PRIMARY_CNS_LYMPHOMA_B_CELL for lineage details; CNS-restricted disease has distinct tropism-defining biology, but specific homing programs are not established as routine clinical biomarkers
